watchlist.thesis: Procter & Gamble remains the cleanest defensive momentum setup in the StockLens screen, with an 88 technical score, 86 risk score and 88 macro score despite weak sentiment.
Visa combines an 86 technical score, 88 risk score and solid composite, but today's post-market earnings event makes the setup explicitly gap-sensitive.
Texas Instruments is a strong liquid semiconductor setup with a 77 composite, 79 technical score, 81 fundamental score and 86 risk score, offset by bearish macro conditions.
Cisco has an 85 technical score, 86 risk score and neutral macro backdrop, making it a cleaner technology trend candidate than many AI-infrastructure names.
Microsoft retains strong fundamentals and a 79 technical score, but its October 28 earnings event and strongly bearish macro score make pre-report entries high-risk.
CrowdStrike remains a high-relative-strength cybersecurity leader with an 87 technical score, but weak macro and risk scores argue for pullback entries only.
Palo Alto Networks remains a liquid cybersecurity momentum candidate with bullish technical structure, but weaker fundamentals and event risk require confirmation.
Palantir remains a liquid software momentum candidate with strong technical and fundamental support, although its November 2 earnings event creates a large gap risk.
Apple remains a deep-liquidity mega-cap trend candidate, with its November 2 earnings event the main near-term position-sizing constraint.
Salesforce remains a liquid software candidate for orderly continuation trades as investors separate durable software economics from capital-intensive AI spending.
ServiceNow remains a high-quality cloud-software trend candidate, but its October 28 earnings event makes post-report confirmation preferable.
Cloudflare remains a high-beta software momentum candidate with strong liquidity, best entered after volatility contracts rather than after sharp upside bursts.
Datadog remains a liquid observability leader that can benefit if software breadth stabilizes, but its November 4 earnings event adds gap risk.
Veeva offers liquid healthcare-software diversification and a cleaner business-model exposure while broad technology leadership remains selective.
Exxon retains an 86 technical and 86 risk score, but its composite fell to 65 with a strongly bearish macro score, so energy exposure should be tactical rather than broad-based.
Chevron remains a liquid energy momentum name with an 86 technical and 87 risk score, although macro conditions are strongly bearish and earnings arrive October 30.
ConocoPhillips remains a liquid upstream energy candidate aligned with current energy strength, with crude reversals and November 5 earnings as the main risks.
EOG provides liquid exploration-and-production exposure to the energy leadership theme, with commodity reversals and November 5 earnings limiting pre-event conviction.
GE Vernova offers liquid power-infrastructure exposure to the AI electricity-buildout theme, but its October 28 pre-market earnings event makes immediate entry gap-sensitive.
Coca-Cola provides a defensive trend anchor with a 74 technical score, 87 risk score and 88 macro score while high-beta technology remains volatile.

sector_notes: The October 27 tape is a rebound within a fragile regime: Reuters reports Monday's S&P 500 and Nasdaq gains were helped by Anthropic's IPO filing, while investors still face hyperscaler earnings and a Federal Reserve decision this week. AI sentiment has improved, but the financing question remains unresolved after Meta's planned equity raise and renewed concern over AI infrastructure returns; semiconductor and neocloud volatility therefore remains elevated. StockLens shows the strongest current technical readings in PG, CRWD, CVX, V, XOM and CSCO, while TXN stands out for the best combination of technical, fundamental and risk scores among semiconductors. Alpha Vantage's news-sentiment endpoint was rate-limited on this run, so the sector read uses the available current market/news sources rather than inventing ticker-level sentiment scores.

avoid.reason: AI sentiment has rebounded but financing and return-on-capex concerns remain unresolved, so require sustained relative strength before treating Nvidia as a fresh swing entry.
Broad AI-infrastructure financing concerns remain a sector headwind despite strategic demand, making confirmed continuation preferable to anticipation.
Alpha Vantage places AMD's earnings on November 3 and the stock remains highly sensitive to AI and semiconductor expectations, so pre-event risk/reward is poor.
Marvell remains tightly exposed to the AI-infrastructure spending and semiconductor-capex debate, which is still producing outsized volatility.
Alpha Vantage places Applied Materials' earnings on November 12; semiconductor-capex uncertainty makes a pre-event momentum entry unattractive.
KLA reports October 28 and remains coupled to the volatile semiconductor-capex regime, so wait for post-event relative-strength confirmation.
Lam Research remains tightly coupled to semiconductor-capex sentiment and the recent AI-driven selloff, so sustained relative strength is required.
Intel combines semiconductor volatility with an October 29 earnings catalyst, leaving a less clean risk-adjusted swing setup.
Alphabet has a major October 28 earnings catalyst and current AI-spending uncertainty makes an event-driven entry less attractive than waiting for the report.
Meta's large planned equity raise for AI infrastructure keeps capital intensity and financing risk in focus despite renewed AI optimism.
CoreWeave remains exposed to debt and AI-infrastructure financing concerns and has a high-volatility profile inconsistent with a clean momentum setup.
Neocloud and AI-infrastructure financing concerns remain a major risk factor, making IREN less attractive than the higher-quality liquid setups on the watchlist.
